subtopic: Geometry of Complex Numbers (Argand Geometry & Loci)
title: Worked (JEE Advanced): an arg-locus is an arc

board_content.text: A constant argument gives a semicircle
A constant argument of $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ means the segment from $-1$ to $1$ subtends a right angle at $z$.
Points where a fixed segment subtends $90^{\circ}$ lie on the circle with that segment as diameter.
It is an ARC (a semicircle), not the whole circle.
The sign $+\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ selects the upper half, $\operatorname{Im}(z)>0$, endpoints excluded.
So: the open upper unit semicircle.

segments_english.text: <curious>What curve do you get when an argument is held constant?</curious> Let's work it out.
Find the locus of z for which the argument of z minus one, over z plus one, equals pi over two.

A constant argument of pi over two means the directed angle from the vector z plus one to the vector z minus one is a right angle. In other words, the segment from minus one to one subtends ninety degrees at z.
And there's a classical fact: the set of points at which a fixed segment subtends a right angle is the circle having that segment as a diameter.
Here the segment runs from minus one to one, so the circle is the unit circle, modulus of z equals one, with that segment as its diameter.
But be careful: a fixed argument gives only an arc, a semicircle, not the whole circle. Half the circle would give the opposite sign of the angle.
The plus sign, plus pi over two, selects the upper half, where the imaginary part of z is positive, and the two endpoints are excluded because the ratio is undefined there.
So the final locus is the open upper half of the unit circle — an arc, exactly as the arg-locus rule warns.

segments_hinglish.text: <curious>Jab ek argument constant rakha jaaye to kaunsa curve milta hai?</curious> Chalo nikaalte hain.
z ka locus nikaalo jiske liye z minus one, over z plus one, ka argument barabar pi over two ho.

Pi over two ka constant argument matlab z plus one vector se z minus one vector tak ka directed angle ek right angle hai. Doosre shabdon mein, minus one se one tak ka segment z par ninety degrees subtend karta hai.
Aur ek classical fact hai: wo points ka set jahan ek fixed segment right angle subtend karta hai, wo circle hai jiska diameter wahi segment ho.
Yahan segment minus one se one tak chalta hai, to circle hai unit circle, modulus of z barabar one, us segment ko apna diameter banate hue.
Par savdhaan: fixed argument sirf ek arc deta hai, ek semicircle, poora circle nahi. Aadha circle angle ka opposite sign deta.
Plus sign, plus pi over two, upper half select karta hai, jahan z ka imaginary part positive hai, aur do endpoints exclude hain kyunki wahan ratio undefined hai.
To final locus hai unit circle ka open upper half — ek arc, bilkul jaisa arg-locus rule warn karta hai.
